options: Keep every prompt short enough to fit on a postcard
Only use AI assistants for casual, everyday topics
Send important prompts twice and compare the answers
Write as if your message could be read by someone else
questions.explain: The postcard rule means writing as if someone else could read your message, which keeps you careful by default about what you share.

questions.q: You want help writing a tricky email about a client's situation. What's the safest way to ask?
options: Include the client's full name, address and account number for accuracy
Swap identifying details for a description like "a small-business owner in Ohio"
Don't use AI at all, because sensitive topics can never be discussed
Paste everything in now and just delete the chat history afterwards
questions.explain: You can still get help with sensitive topics by removing or swapping identifying details. A general description works just as well as a name and address.

questions.q: You're about to download an AI assistant app on your phone. What should you check first?
options: That the app has the word "AI" in its name
That it lists the most features in the store
That the developer is the official company
That it charges a fee, since free apps are fakes
questions.explain: The lesson says to use the official app and check the developer name carefully, because copycat apps exist and some charge for things that are free.
